original_question: Let sigma be a continuous Borel measure on the unit circle, and let T be an ergodic Gaussian automorphism whose spectrum contains sigma as a component; when sigma is singular, such a Gaussian automorphism has zero entropy. Do zero-entropy ergodic Gaussian automorphisms satisfy all of the properties S_n, where S_n means that every n-fold self-joining whose projections to all (n - 1)-dimensional faces equal mu^{n-1} is trivial?
target_in_paper: §2, Q11 (the Gaussian special case of the del Junco–Rudolph problem): “Do ergodic Gaussian automorphisms with zero entropy have the properties S_n?” The paper asks this immediately after recalling that every continuous Borel measure on the unit circle occurs as a spectral component of some ergodic Gaussian automorphism, and that singular such measures yield zero entropy. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2405.03641v1))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the paper’s zero-entropy Gaussian special case, and your informal meaning of S_n matches the §2 joining definition: an n-fold self-joining whose projections to all (n-1)-dimensional coordinate faces are the product measure must itself be the full product joining. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2405.03641v1))
missing_details: The official paper target is Q11 in §2, not the broader Q9; Q11 is presented as a special Gaussian case of the del Junco–Rudolph zero-entropy/PID problem. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2405.03641v1))

The formal hypothesis in Q11 is simply “ergodic Gaussian automorphisms with zero entropy”; the preceding sentence about a continuous Borel measure σ on the unit circle is motivation, not part of the quantifier of the official question. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2405.03641v1))

To be fully stand-alone, the question should specify a probability-preserving system (X, B, μ, T), and that the self-joinings are n-fold self-joinings of copies of T, invariant under the diagonal action. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2405.03641v1))

The family S_n is indexed for n>2; the paper then uses PID for the conjunction of all these properties. That range of n is implicit in your draft and should be stated explicitly. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2405.03641v1))

A paper-faithful formulation should mention the equivalent shorthand PID = ⋂_{n>2} S_n, since the surrounding context frames Q11 as a special case of the del Junco–Rudolph PID question. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2405.03641v1))

Your mention of singular σ should not replace the actual Q11 hypothesis by “continuous singular spectrum”: nearby Theorem 2.2 proves all S_n under the stronger assumption of continuous singular spectrum, whereas Q11 is asked under the weaker hypothesis of zero entropy for Gaussian automorphisms. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2405.03641v1))
refined_question: Let (X, B, μ, T) be an ergodic Gaussian automorphism of a probability space with zero Kolmogorov–Sinai entropy. For each n>2, say that T has property S_n if every n-fold self-joining λ of T whose projection to every (n-1)-dimensional coordinate face is μ^{⊗(n-1)} is necessarily λ = μ^{⊗ n}. Must every zero-entropy ergodic Gaussian automorphism satisfy S_n for every n>2? ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2405.03641v1))
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently: does every ergodic Gaussian automorphism with zero entropy have the PID property, i.e. belong to ⋂_{n>2} S_n? ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2405.03641v1))
justification: This rewrite stays closest to Q11 itself. The paper first defines the joining properties S_n in §2 and notes that PID means satisfying all of them. It then states the broader del Junco–Rudolph problem Q9 for zero-entropy weakly mixing automorphisms, and immediately singles out Q11 as the Gaussian special case. The nearby Theorem 2.2 gives a positive answer under the stronger hypothesis of continuous singular spectrum, which explains why your draft’s mention of singular spectral measures is relevant background, but not the official formal statement. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2405.03641v1))
